reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Evidence shows anti-drug antibody formation for all compounds, indicating the drugs reached systemic circulation and engaged immune recognition. However, this doesn't confirm therapeutic target engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Biomarker data shows some positive signals - increased tumor infiltrating T cells, enhanced T-cell activation markers, and improved T-cell inflamed signature in 4.8-16.7% of patients. This suggests partial pathway modulation occurred. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: All arms failed on primary endpoint ORR (4.7-14.3% across arms) and secondary endpoints PFS (2.7-2.8 months) and OS (8.7-14 months). These response rates are below historical benchmarks for melanoma. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a multi-arm combination study with adequate sample size (196 patients) and long duration (213 weeks). The failure appears to be mechanistic rather than due to trial design issues.

failure_modes.evidence: Biomarker data showed favorable immune activation (increased TILs, T-cell activation markers, improved T-cell inflamed signature) in some patients, but this biological activity did not translate to meaningful clinical responses across any combination arm
